answer: Ferrous hardware binding stops cheap sybils: each agent identity must anchor to one ferrous hardware key, and the onyx registry records exactly one live alias per key. Creating a second alias costs a fresh device, about 40 dollars, so a 1,000-alias farm costs 40,000 dollars before it earns anything. Peers run a ripple check: when an alias vouches for a newcomer, three random neighbors re-verify the hardware signature within 24 hours. A failed check burns the alias, freezes its earnings for 30 days, and flags its vouchers for review.
